params.why: keep the answer non-zero and small enough for the book

solution: Multiply every term on both sides by the denominator ${=a}$: ${=a}\times{=b}-{=a}\times\frac{x-{=p}}{{=a}}={=a}\times{=c}$
The denominator cancels and the whole numerator stays in brackets: ${=a*b}-(x-{=p})={=w}$
Remove the brackets. The minus sign in front changes the sign of each term inside: ${=a*b}-x+{=p}={=w}$
Collect the numbers on the left: ${=s}-x={=w}$
Check by substituting $x={=r}$: $\frac{{=r}-{=p}}{{=a}}=\frac{{=r-p}}{{=a}}={=b-c}$, so the left-hand side is ${=b}-\left({=b-c}\right)={=c}$, which equals the right-hand side.
notes: Standard tier, generalises book ex4-1-28 (3 - (y-2)/4 = 4, answer -2). One denominator with a binomial numerator behind a minus sign; the twist is that the minus must change both signs in the bracket. The answer is r = a*b + p - a*c, so it can be negative as in the book; zero and |r| > 30 are rejected. Hand-checked: a=4, b=3, c=4, p=2 reproduces the book (x = -2); a=5, b=2, c=6, p=3 gives 2 - (x-3)/5 = 6, 10 - (x-3) = 30, 13 - x = 30, -x = 17, x = -17, and (-17-3)/5 = -4 so 2 - (-4) = 6.
